title: Access onboarding + service account states — sketches & grooming notes
content:
Context / goal:
- Consolidate org/team onboarding flows: invite users, assign roles, create service accounts, provision API keys, and surface audit-trail during onboarding.
- Make flows frictionless for engineering teams adopting Redwood Dedicated/Private where service accounts are common (CI, infra, pipeline runs).
- Capture wireframe states we sketched in the whiteboard session on 2025-11-10 and convert into backlog-ready items.

Audience:
- Primary: product-console PMs and UX engineers.
- Secondary: eng infra + security for constraints (KMS integration, rotation window), Solutions Eng for enterprise expectations.

High level UX principles to follow (quick reminders):
- Make the minimum safe default the path of least resistance: "Create user with read-only" vs "Admin" should require an explicit step.
- Surface consequences: when creating API key / service account, show where it will be used and retention window.
- Inline help for templates (pipeline, monitoring, deployment) — link to example terraform/snippets.
- Auditability and explainability: every step should log an auditable event and surface expected entry in the audit log preview.

User journeys captured here (sketchy, prioritize):
1) New org admin wants to onboard a partner engineering team.
   - Steps: Invite user(s) -> create team -> assign role templated (devops/dev) -> optionally create service account with scoped keys -> send email w/ one-time key.
   - Key UX requirements: bulk invite, role templates, preview of access (table), do-not-block on key creation but warn about ephemeral exposure.

2) SRE pipeline needs a service account for CI -> requires non-human account + rotating key + least privilege.
   - Steps: Create service account -> select policies (scoped to project/model/specific routes) -> generate API key -> provide immediate download option and copy-once warning -> configure rotation policy (recommended: 30d) -> schedule rotation job (link to infra-runbook).
   - Acceptance: role/route scoping UI must be fine-grained (model-level + route-level) and show token rate-limits preview.

Wireframe states (descriptions; label consistency: Onboard > Roles > Keys > Audit Preview):
- Onboard start card
  - Title: "Get your team running"
  - CTA: Invite user | Create service account
  - Quick checklist: Invite, set role template, optional SA & API key, review audit preview
  - Tiny link: "Use terraform instead" -> expands overlay with snippet and example provider config

- Invite modal (bulk)
  - Input: comma-separated emails + CSV upload
  - Role dropdown: template (Dev, SRE, Billing, Read-only) + advanced chooser -> opens permissions matrix
  - Option checkbox: "Require SSO" (checked by default for enterprise orgs)
  - After submit: ephemeral toast with link to pending invites and audit event (INVITE_CREATED)

- Role template editor (mini modal)
  - Left: role name + description
  - Middle: permissions matrix (routes x actions), checkboxes per route group
  - Right: suggested least-privilege recommendations (auto-suggest based on role intent)
  - Save creates role-template object; note: this is currently stored in org config (backlog item: make templates exportable/importable)

- Service account creation flow (multi-step inline)
  - Step 1: Identity -> name + intended use (dropdown: ci/cd, batch-job, external-integration)
  - Step 2: Scope -> select teams/projects/models/routes (searchable tag input). Default: "same as creator's team".
  - Step 3: Key policy -> Single key | Rotating keys (recommended) | External KMS-only
  - Step 4: Output -> download key (one-time) OR send to secure vault (Hashi/Secrets Manager integration)
  - Visual indicators: "Risk" badge if broad wildcard scope used; tooltip explaining impact

- API key generation inline behavior
  - Copy-once modal: displays token, expiration, and cli example. Buttons: Copy, Download JSON, Send-to-Vault.
  - If rotating keys chosen: show rotation schedule summary and sample curl to rotate.

- Audit preview panel (right rail)
  - Shows recent events filtered to the resource being created (INVITE_CREATED, SA_CREATED, API_KEY_ISSUED)
  - Example rows: date, actor, action, target, IP (if available), ticket-id (optional)
  - Filter chips: show only errors, show only admin actions, show only keys
  - Link: "Open full audit" -> opens full console audit view

Error and edge cases we sketched:
- Lost API key: flow to revoke and reissue a new rotating key; immediate audit event and notification to team slack.
- Bulk invite fail partially: show summary of failure reasons inline with CSV row numbers.
- Service account with cross-org scope: blocked by default unless enterprise opt-in; require additional review ticket.
- KMS-only keys: users selecting this must enter KMS key-id and we persist a reference only; UX needs inline validation from KMS API call.

Open questions / unresolved design choices:
- Should role templates be org-scoped only, or shareable across teams? (Tradeoffs: discoverability vs accidental privilege blur)
- Naming convention enforcement for SAs? (e.g., sa-{team}-{purpose}) — should we auto-suggest and validate uniqueness?
- How much of policy editing should be exposed to non-admins? We sketched a "request changes" flow where team leads can request elevated perms that create a review ticket — do we want that initial MVP?
- Audit preview sampling: what retention and sampling threshold do we show in the small preview vs the full audit console? (Ask SRE/security about retention costs.)

Backlog / actionable tickets to create (prioritized):
- MUST: Bulk invite UI -> CSV import + partial failure handling (ticket: CON-INV-142)
- SHOULD: Service account multi-step flow + copy-once key modal + vault integration (ticket: CON-SA-58)
- SHOULD: Role template editor (mini) with least-privilege suggestions (CON-ROLE-77)
- SHOULD: Audit preview right-rail for onboarding flows (CON-AUD-31)
- MAYBE: Auto-suggest SA naming + enforcement (CON-SA-99)

Accessibility notes:
- Ensure modal forms are keyboard-trappable; copy-once modal must announce using screen reader when token created (ARIA live region saying "API key created, copy now").
- Color contrast for risk badges (red/orange) should meet AA.

Implementation constraints / backend considerations (notes for ENG):
- API endpoints expected: /orgs/{org}/invites (bulk), /orgs/{org}/service-accounts (create + policy), /audit/events?filter=resource
- We should store only key-hash in our audit logs for security; full plaintext stored only in transient store and served once.
- KMS integration: fetch key metadata at creation time for validation; do not persist plaintext KMS material.
- Rate-limit implications: generating keys at scale could hit key-store quotas (SRE to confirm)

Design notes / micro-interactions:
- Inline permission preview: show a small "What this role means" summary (2-line) when you hover a role template.
- Onboarding checklist can be public link for partners (read-only view showing granted permissions and contact).
- Provide a one-click "revoke all keys for this SA" action on the SA card; requires confirmation and creates audit event.

Sketch (ascii wireframe, very rough):

[Onboard card]        | [Right rail: Audit preview]
----------------------|-------------------------
Title: Get your team   | 2025-11-10  14:22  SA_CREATED  Maya
CTA Invite | Create SA | 2025-11-10  14:23  API_KEY_ISSUED  CI-pipeline
Checklist:             | Filter: [keys] [admin]
- Invite users          | Link: Open full audit
- Set role template     |
- Optional: create SA   |

Testing plan (manual):
- QA checklist for feature: invite flow success, partial CSV failures shown, SA creation returns single-use key and cannot be retrieved again, audit event appears in preview and full audit console.
- Security review: ensure key copy is one-time, no logs of plaintext keys in system logs, penetration test for SA creation endpoint.

Next steps (immediate):
- PM (Maya) to open tickets for MUST/SHOULD items and assign owners (Jonas: bulk invite; Rosa: SA flow; Samir: audit preview).
- UX: produce mid-fidelity mockups for the SA creation flow and audit preview (deadline: 2025-12-12).
- ENG: sync with SRE on KMS and key rotation quotas (meeting: 2025-12-03)

Notes to self (choppy/thoughts):
- Keep the invite modal light — most orgs will do 1-3 invites at a time; CSV exists for enterprise on-boarding.
- Rotation: default to 30d but allow org override; show cost of rotation in UI? maybe later.
- Consider modal telemetry: which CTAs get clicked more -> to inform defaults.

-- end --
